series.title: Real GDP growth
series.sub: Annualized change from the prior quarter
series.note: Chained 2017 dollars. Each quarter is revised twice after the advance estimate; the third estimate arrives about three months after the quarter ends.

series.title: Nominal GDP
series.sub: Current dollars, seasonally adjusted annual rate
series.note: The level series is the denominator for the debt and deficit ratios below. Use the log scale to read growth rates off the slope.

meta.title: Gross Domestic Product

series.title: Labor productivity growth
series.sub: Nonfarm business output per hour, change from a year earlier
series.note: Computed here as the four-quarter change in the output-per-hour index.

meta.title: Nonfarm Business Sector: Labor Productivity (Output per Hour) for All Workers

series.title: Labor share of income
series.sub: Compensation of employees as a share of gross domestic income
series.note: The remainder of gross domestic income goes to proprietors, corporate profits, interest, rents, production taxes, and depreciation; the income-by-type tile breaks it out. Gross domestic income arrives with the second GDP estimate, so this lags real GDP growth by a month.

meta.title: Gross Domestic Income: Compensation of Employees, Paid

series.title: Unemployment rate
series.sub: Civilian labor force, ages 16 and over
series.note: From the household survey. The broader U-6 measure, which adds discouraged and involuntary part-time workers, can be added as a companion tile.

meta.title: Unemployment Rate

series.title: Labor force participation
series.sub: Share of the population aged 16 and over in the labor force
series.note: The long decline since 2000 is mostly aging; the prime-age rate next door strips that out.

meta.title: Labor Force Participation Rate

series.title: Prime-age employment rate
series.sub: Employed share of the population aged 25 to 54

meta.title: Employment-Population Ratio - 25-54 Yrs.

series.title: Payroll employment, monthly change
series.sub: Total nonfarm, thousands of jobs
series.note: First-differenced from the payroll level. The two most recent months are preliminary and get revised with each release. April 2020 dwarfs everything else; a range button trims it.

meta.title: All Employees, Total Nonfarm

series.title: Participation rate by sex
series.sub: Share of the population aged 16 and over in the labor force
series.note: The two rates converged for fifty years and have moved roughly together since 2000. Prime-age versions by sex can be added as a companion tile.

meta.title: Labor Force Participation Rate - Men

series.title: Total public debt

series.note: The headline figure often quoted as "the national debt." About a fifth of it is held in government accounts such as the Social Security trust funds; the debt held by the public tile is the part owed to outside lenders and the one that drives interest costs.

comp.freq_label: Monthly, accumulated over the fiscal year (October to September)
comp.note: The snapshot is the current fiscal year to date and compares with the same months a year earlier; once the September statement posts in mid-October it covers the full year. The history uses complete fiscal years, which on FiscalData begin with 2016. Medicare is shown gross of premiums; Medicaid sits inside Health.

comp.title: Income side of GDP, by type
comp.sub: Gross domestic income by type of income, NIPA table 1.10
comp.note: Compensation is labor income; corporate profits, net interest, rental income, and depreciation are returns to capital; proprietors' income mixes the two. Everything else is business transfer payments and the surplus of government enterprises. The latest quarter shown is the most recent with all components published; gross domestic income arrives a month after the advance GDP estimate.

comp.title: Payroll employment by sector
comp.note: Establishment survey. Education and health services is the private-sector supersector; public schools and hospitals sit in government.

comp.title: Labor force by sex
comp.sub: Civilian labor force, ages 16 and over
comp.note: Household survey. Women's share of the labor force rose from about 30 percent in 1948 to roughly 47 percent by 2000 and has been flat since.
